title: The Morning Digest: October 1, 2026
dek: Gulf crude flows are back near pre-war levels and Brent fell to ~$96 in Asia before recovering; the product market is in full distress with record cracks. TMW Nov26 tightened 50c to -$21.60 while December sits widest at -$22.40, staring at the 40-million-barrel SPR exchange.

Products - the binding constraint: NYMEX diesel crack back above $100/bbl (most of September; first crossed Apr 2022); European diesel cracks >$100 vs North Sea. RBN (9/30): 3-2-1 crack at an all-time high $80.63; gasoline inventories at 204 Mbbl, lowest since Nov 2014; PADD 2 gasoline at a record low.
Products - the binding constraint: Policy risk is rising on the demand side:

Products - the binding constraint: The Gulf product problem is the mirror image of the crude recovery: Hormuz crude is back, but Gulf diesel/gasoil exports are a fraction of February levels, IEA refinery runs are below last year, and Russian refineries are still being hit by Ukrainian strikes. Crude is a liquid market; products are a stranded one.

Venezuela - the blockade is now a campaign: Vortexa (presented Sep 29) estimates ~20% of Venezuela's seaborne crude exports have moved into Caribbean storage (Bahamas, Curaçao, St. Lucia) since the blockade began - marketed for sale by Trafigura and Vitol. Chevron-license exports to the US continue in parallel; US naphtha still flows to Venezuela as diluent.

Venezuela - the blockade is now a campaign: Caracas hosted a sold-out oil summit Sep 29 - 30 (250+ companies, 600+ delegates); Exxon is reportedly nearing a preliminary agreement to return to Venezuelan fields (~20 years after the 2007 nationalization); Qatar's UCC is in talks to enter.
